source.text: אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר שְׁלֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְרַעְנַ֖ן בְּהֵיכְלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I, Nebuchadnezzar, at ease was in my house and flourishing in my palace.

en.L: I, Nebuchadnezzar, at ease I was in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
en.B: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was living at ease in my house, prospering in my palace.
en.R: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at home in my palace. I was happy, and everything was going well for me.

pt.L: Eu, Nabucodonosor, estava tranquilo na minha casa e florescente no meu palácio.
pt.B: Eu, Nabucodonosor, vivia tranquilo na minha casa, próspero no meu palácio.
pt.R: Eu, Nabucodonosor, estava em casa, no meu palácio. Eu estava feliz, e tudo ia bem para mim.

decisions.choice: This verse is 4:1 in the Aramaic text, 4:4 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: In the Aramaic text, chapter 4 begins here, after the opening of the king's letter (3:31-33). Many Bibles number the letter's opening 4:1-3, so their 4:4-37 is 4:1-34 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the text it translates, and cites chapter 4 that way.

decisions.choice: I, Nebuchadnezzar: the king tells his own story
decisions.reason: The chapter is the body of the letter begun in 3:31, told in the king's own words. In verses 16-30 the story speaks of him as "the king" and "he"; in verse 31 it returns to "I". Such a change of person happens in ancient royal inscriptions too.

decisions.choice: at ease ... flourishing: secure and prosperous
decisions.reason: The second word is used of a green, leafy tree (Psalm 52:10; 92:15). It prepares for the tree of the dream: the king is himself the flourishing tree (verse 19).

decisions.choice: I was happy, and everything was going well for me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "at ease" and "flourishing" mean for a person.

decisions.choice: florescente (L); próspero (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "florescente", a word Portuguese uses both for a tree in leaf and for a prosperous man, so that the king's words already point to the tree of the dream (m3); Balanced says "próspero", the sense for a person.

source.text: חֵ֥לֶם חֲזֵ֖ית וִֽידַחֲלִנַּ֑נִי וְהַרְהֹרִין֙ עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֔י וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: A dream I saw, and it made me afraid; and imaginings on my bed and [the] visions of my head alarmed me.

en.L: I saw a dream, and it made me afraid; and the fancies on my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.
en.B: I had a dream that frightened me. As I lay in bed, the images and visions that passed through my mind terrified me.
en.R: Then I had a dream that frightened me. As I lay in bed, the things I saw in my mind terrified me.

pt.L: Vi um sonho, e ele me amedrontou; e as fantasias sobre a minha cama e as visões da minha cabeça me perturbaram.
pt.B: Tive um sonho que me deu medo. Enquanto eu estava deitado, as imagens e as visões que passavam pela minha mente me aterrorizaram.
pt.R: Então tive um sonho que me deu medo. Enquanto eu estava deitado na cama, as coisas que vi na minha mente me deixaram apavorado.

decisions.choice: imaginings: images seen in the mind
decisions.reason: The word is used only here and means fancies or mental pictures, what the mind sees in a dream.

decisions.choice: the visions of my head: what I saw in my mind
decisions.reason: As in 2:28, the head is where one sees in dreams.

decisions.choice: images and visions that passed through my mind (B); things I saw in my mind (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Aramaic phrases mean (m1, m2).

source.text: וּמִנִּי֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְהַנְעָלָ֣ה קָֽדָמַ֔י לְכֹ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֑ל דִּֽי־פְשַׁ֥ר חֶלְמָ֖א יְהֽוֹדְעֻנַּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And from me was made a decree to bring in before me all [the] wise men of Babylon, that the interpretation of the dream they might make known to me.

en.L: And a decree was issued from me to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, so that the interpretation of the dream they might make known to me.
en.B: So I gave orders for all the wise men of Babylon to be brought before me to tell me what the dream meant.
en.R: So I ordered that all the wise men of Babylon be brought to me. I wanted them to tell me what my dream meant.

pt.L: E da minha parte foi feito um decreto para trazer diante de mim todos os sábios da Babilônia, para que me fizessem conhecer a interpretação do sonho.
pt.B: Por isso dei ordem para que todos os sábios da Babilônia fossem trazidos à minha presença, para me dizerem o que o sonho significava.
pt.R: Então mandei que todos os sábios da Babilônia fossem trazidos até mim. Eu queria que eles me dissessem o que o meu sonho significava.

decisions.choice: all the wise men of Babylon: as in chapter 2
decisions.reason: The king does what he did in chapter 2, but this time he tells the dream (verse 4). Even so, his experts fail, and only Daniel can interpret.

decisions.choice: I issued a decree (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the Aramaic passive, "a decree was made from me", into the active.

source.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן עָלִּ֗ין חַרְטֻמַיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א כַּשְׂדָּאֵ֖י וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א וְחֶלְמָ֗א אָמַ֤ר אֲנָה֙ קֳדָ֣מֵיה֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לָא־מְהוֹדְעִ֥ין לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Then came in the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners, and the dream I told before them, and its interpretation not were they making known to me.

en.L: Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners came in, and I told the dream before them, but its interpretation they could not make known to me.
en.B: Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans and diviners came in, and I told them the dream, but they could not tell me what it meant.
en.R: Then the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners came. I told them my dream, but they could not tell me what it meant.

pt.L: Então entraram os magos, os encantadores, os caldeus e os adivinhos, e eu contei o sonho diante deles, mas a sua interpretação eles não me fizeram conhecer.
pt.B: Então vieram os magos, os encantadores, os caldeus e os adivinhos, e eu lhes contei o sonho, mas eles não conseguiram me dizer o que ele significava.
pt.R: Então vieram os magos, os encantadores, os astrólogos e os adivinhos. Contei a eles o meu sonho, mas eles não conseguiram me dizer o que ele significava.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans and the diviners: classes of experts
decisions.reason: As in 2:2 and 2:27, "Chaldeans" here names a class of experts, not the people. The four groups are the experts of chapter 2, and the list is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: they could not make known: they failed even though they knew the dream
decisions.reason: In chapter 2 the experts said that they could interpret if the king told them the dream (2:4, 7). Now he tells it, and they still cannot.

decisions.choice: the list kept at every level; astrologers (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms for Daniel set, the list of experts is kept at every level, with "astrologers" at Readable for the Chaldeans as a class of experts.

source.text: וְעַ֣ד אָחֳרֵ֡ין עַל֩ קָֽדָמַ֨י דָּנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־שְׁמֵ֤הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ כְּשֻׁ֣ם אֱלָהִ֔י וְדִ֛י רֽוּחַ־אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בֵּ֑הּ וְחֶלְמָ֖א קָֽדָמ֥וֹהִי אַמְרֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And until last came in before me Daniel, whose name [was] Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god, and in whom a spirit of gods holy [is], and the dream before him I told:

en.L: And at last there came in before me Daniel, whose name [is] Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god, who has in him a spirit of [the] holy gods; and the dream I told before him:
en.B: At last Daniel came in before me. He is called Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him the dream:
en.R: At last Daniel came to me. I had named him Belteshazzar, after the name of my god. The spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him my dream.

pt.L: E por fim entrou diante de mim Daniel, cujo nome [é] Beltessazar, segundo o nome do meu deus, e em quem há um espírito [dos] deuses santos; e eu contei o sonho diante dele:
pt.B: Por fim, Daniel veio à minha presença. Ele se chama Beltessazar, por causa do nome do meu deus, e o espírito dos deuses santos está nele. Eu lhe contei o sonho:
pt.R: Por fim, Daniel veio até mim. Eu tinha dado a ele o nome de Beltessazar, por causa do nome do meu deus. O espírito dos deuses santos está nele. Contei a ele o meu sonho.

decisions.choice: after the name of my god: Bel, the god of Babylon
decisions.reason: The king links Belteshazzar with Bel, a title of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon (Isaiah 46:1; Jeremiah 50:2). The name is probably the Babylonian "Balatsu-usur", "protect his life"; the king hears in it his god's name (see 1:7).

decisions.choice: a spirit of the holy gods: the king's way of speaking of God's gift to Daniel
alternatives: the spirit of the holy God
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word for "gods" is plural. In the mouth of a polytheist king it most likely means "the holy gods", as the plural adjective "holy" suggests (verses 6, 15; 5:11, 14). The Hebrew word for God is also plural in form, and some read "the spirit of the holy God". The reader knows that Daniel's wisdom comes from the God of Israel (1:17; 2:19-23).

decisions.choice: at last: after all the others had failed
decisions.reason: The words may mean that Daniel came "last" or "finally", perhaps after the king had tried the others first. The text does not explain why Daniel was not called at once.

decisions.choice: a spirit of [the] holy gods (L); the spirit of the holy gods (B, R); lowercase
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the plural "gods" and lowercase, since these are a polytheist's words (m2). Readable says "I had named him", since the king (or his officer, 1:7) gave Daniel the name.

decisions.choice: um espírito [dos] deuses santos (L); o espírito dos deuses santos (B, R); lowercase
decisions.reason: As the English, every level keeps the plural "deuses" and lowercase "espírito", since these are a polytheist king's words (m2); the same wording returns in verses 6 and 15 and in 5:11, 14.

source.text: בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֮ רַ֣ב חַרְטֻמַיָּא֒ דִּ֣י׀אֲנָ֣ה יִדְעֵ֗ת דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֤ין קַדִּישִׁין֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְכָל־רָ֖ז לָא־אָנֵ֣ס לָ֑ךְ חֶזְוֵ֨י חֶלְמִ֧י דִֽי־חֲזֵ֛ית וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ אֱמַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, whom I know that a spirit of gods holy [is] in you, and any secret not troubles you: [the] visions of my dream that I saw and its interpretation tell.

en.L: "Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that a spirit of [the] holy gods [is] in you, and no secret is too hard for you, tell [me] the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation.
en.B: "Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I am sure that the spirit of the holy gods is within you and that no mystery is too hard for you. Here are the visions I saw in my dream; tell me what they mean.
en.R: "Belteshazzar, you are the leader of all the magicians. I know that the spirit of the holy gods lives in you. I know that no secret is too hard for you to explain. Here is what I saw in my dream. Tell me what it means.

pt.L: "Beltessazar, chefe dos magos, porque eu sei que um espírito [dos] deuses santos [está] em você, e nenhum segredo é difícil demais para você, diga as visões do meu sonho que eu vi e a sua interpretação.
pt.B: "Beltessazar, chefe dos magos, tenho certeza de que o espírito dos deuses santos está em você e de que nenhum mistério é difícil demais para você. Estas são as visões que tive no meu sonho; diga-me o que elas significam.
pt.R: "Beltessazar, você é o chefe de todos os magos. Eu sei que o espírito dos deuses santos vive em você. Sei que nenhum segredo é difícil demais para você explicar. Isto é o que eu vi no meu sonho. Diga-me o que significa.

decisions.choice: chief of the magicians: the head of the king's experts
decisions.reason: This was Daniel's position after chapter 2, where he was made chief over all the wise men of Babylon (2:48). The king names him by the first group of the list.

decisions.choice: no secret troubles you: no mystery is too hard for you
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or to be too hard for someone. The king trusts Daniel's gift.

decisions.choice: tell the visions of my dream: tell me what the visions mean
alternatives: tell me the visions of my dream (as in chapter 2)
decisions.reason: The king has already told the dream (verse 5); here he asks for its meaning, as verse 15 makes plain. The Aramaic is compressed: "the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation, tell".

decisions.choice: Here are the visions ...; tell me what they mean (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the king tells the dream and asks for its meaning (m3). The king's account of the dream that follows is a quotation of what he said to Daniel, so it opens with a quotation mark.

source.text: וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וַאֲל֥וּ אִילָ֛ן בְּג֥וֹא אַרְעָ֖א וְרוּמֵ֥הּ שַׂגִּֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] visions of my head upon my bed, seeing I was, and look, a tree in [the] midst of the earth, and its height [was] great.

en.L: And the visions of my head upon my bed: I was looking, and there was a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height [was] great.
en.B: These were the visions that passed through my mind as I lay in bed: I looked, and there before me was a tree in the middle of the earth, and it was very tall.
en.R: This is what I saw while I was lying in bed: I saw a very tall tree in the middle of the world.

pt.L: E as visões da minha cabeça sobre a minha cama: eu estava olhando, e havia uma árvore no meio da terra, e a sua altura [era] grande.
pt.B: Estas foram as visões que passaram pela minha mente quando eu estava deitado: eu olhei, e diante de mim havia uma árvore no meio da terra, e ela era muito alta.
pt.R: Isto foi o que eu vi enquanto estava deitado na cama: vi uma árvore muito alta no meio do mundo.

decisions.choice: a tree in the midst of the earth: a picture of a great king
decisions.reason: A great tree is a picture of a mighty king or empire in Ezekiel 17:22-24 and 31:3-14, where Assyria is a cedar whose top reached the clouds and in whose shade all nations lived. Ancient peoples also spoke of a world tree at the center of the earth. The dream draws on such pictures; verse 19 says that the tree is the king.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole world
decisions.reason: The word can mean "land" or "earth"; the tree that is seen "to the end of all the earth" (verse 8) stands at the center of the world.

decisions.choice: world (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "world" to show that the tree stands at the center of everything (m2).

source.text: רְבָ֥ה אִֽילָנָ֖א וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְס֥וֹף כָּל־אַרְעָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Grew the tree and became strong, and its height reached to the heavens, and its sight to [the] end of all the earth.

en.L: The tree grew and became strong, and its height reached to the heavens, and its visibility to the end of all the earth.
en.B: The tree grew large and strong; its top touched the sky, and it could be seen from the ends of the earth.
en.R: The tree grew bigger and stronger. Its top reached up to the sky. People everywhere in the world could see it.

pt.L: A árvore cresceu e se tornou forte, e a sua altura chegava até os céus, e a sua visibilidade até o fim de toda a terra.
pt.B: A árvore cresceu e ficou forte; o seu topo tocava o céu, e ela podia ser vista dos confins da terra.
pt.R: A árvore ficou maior e mais forte. O seu topo chegava até o céu. As pessoas de todos os lugares do mundo podiam vê-la.

decisions.choice: its height reached to the heavens: a picture of pride
decisions.reason: A building or tree that reaches the heavens recalls the tower of Babel (Genesis 11:4), and the cedar of Ezekiel 31:10 whose heart grew proud because of its height. The tree's height shows both the king's greatness and his danger.

decisions.choice: its visibility (L)
decisions.reason: The rare Aramaic word means "its being seen"; Literal says "its visibility", Balanced and Readable "it could be seen".

source.text: עָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֜וֹהִי תַּטְלֵ֣ל׀חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֗א וּבְעַנְפ֨וֹהִי֙ יְדוּרָן֙ צִפֲּרֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א וּמִנֵּ֖הּ יִתְּזִ֥ין כָּל־בִּשְׂרָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Its foliage [was] beautiful, and its fruit abundant, and food for all [was] in it; under it the beasts of the field found shade, and in its branches dwelt the birds of the heavens, and from it was fed all flesh.

en.L: Its foliage [was] beautiful and its fruit abundant, and in it [was] food for all. Under it the animals of the field found shade, and in its branches the birds of the heavens nested, and from it all flesh was fed.
en.B: Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and on it was food for everyone. Wild animals rested in its shade, birds nested in its branches, and every living creature was fed from it.
en.R: It had beautiful leaves and lots of fruit, enough food for everyone. Wild animals rested in its shade. Birds made their nests in its branches. Every living creature ate from it.

pt.L: A sua folhagem [era] bela e o seu fruto abundante, e nela [havia] alimento para todos. Debaixo dela os animais do campo achavam sombra, e nos seus ramos as aves dos céus faziam ninho, e dela se alimentava toda carne.
pt.B: As suas folhas eram belas e os seus frutos abundantes, e nela havia alimento para todos. Os animais selvagens descansavam à sua sombra, as aves faziam ninho nos seus galhos, e todo ser vivo se alimentava dela.
pt.R: Ela tinha folhas bonitas e muitos frutos, comida suficiente para todos. Os animais selvagens descansavam na sua sombra. As aves faziam ninhos nos seus galhos. Todo ser vivo comia dela.

decisions.choice: animals under it, birds in its branches: the king's care for his peoples
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of Assyria's cedar (Ezekiel 31:6) and of the kingdom of God in Jesus' parable of the mustard seed, where the birds of the air nest in its branches (Matthew 13:32). A king was meant to shelter and feed his peoples; the dream shows Nebuchadnezzar's empire as such a tree.

decisions.choice: all flesh: every living creature
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means every living being, animals and people (Genesis 6:17).

decisions.choice: every living creature (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "all flesh" means (m2).

source.text: חָזֵ֥ה הֲוֵ֛ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבִ֑י וַאֲלוּ֙ עִ֣יר וְקַדִּ֔ישׁ מִן־שְׁמַיָּ֖א נָחִֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Seeing I was in [the] visions of my head upon my bed, and look, a watcher and a holy one from the heavens [was] coming down.

en.L: I was looking in the visions of my head upon my bed, and there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens.
en.B: As I lay in bed, I was watching the visions in my mind, and there before me was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
en.R: While I was lying in bed and watching these things in my mind, I saw a heavenly messenger, a holy one, coming down from the sky.

pt.L: Eu estava olhando nas visões da minha cabeça sobre a minha cama, e havia um vigia, um santo, descendo dos céus.
pt.B: Enquanto eu estava deitado, olhando as visões na minha mente, diante de mim havia um vigia, um santo, que descia do céu.
pt.R: Enquanto eu estava deitado na cama vendo essas coisas na minha mente, vi um mensageiro celestial, um santo, descendo do céu.

decisions.choice: a watcher, a holy one: a heavenly being, one of God's attendants
alternatives: a watcher and a holy one (two beings)
decisions.reason: The word *'ir* is found only in this chapter (verses 10, 14, 20) and comes from a root meaning "to be awake". It names a heavenly being who keeps watch, one of the angels who serve God (compare the "holy ones" of Psalm 89:6, 8 and Zechariah 14:5). "A holy one" says the same thing in other words; the "and" joins two names for one being. Later Jewish writings, such as 1 Enoch, use "watchers" for angels, both faithful and fallen.

decisions.choice: coming down from the heavens: a messenger sent from God's court
decisions.reason: The watcher brings a decision made in heaven (verse 14) to the earth. The king's great tree, whose top reached to the heavens (verse 8), meets the one who comes down from them.

decisions.choice: a watcher (L, B); a heavenly messenger (R)
decisions.reason: The terms for Daniel set "a watcher" at Literal and Balanced and "a heavenly messenger" at Readable, which says what a watcher is (m1).

decisions.choice: um vigia (L, B); um mensageiro celestial (R); um santo
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter (verses 14, 20): *'ir* (m1) is "vigia", one who keeps awake and watches, at Literal and Balanced, and "mensageiro celestial" at Readable, as the English says "heavenly messenger". "Anjo" is kept for the word the text uses in 3:28 and 6:23.

source.text: קָרֵ֨א בְחַ֜יִל וְכֵ֣ן אָמַ֗ר גֹּ֤דּוּ אִֽילָנָא֙ וְקַצִּ֣צוּ עַנְפ֔וֹהִי אַתַּ֥רוּ עָפְיֵ֖הּ וּבַדַּ֣רוּ אִנְבֵּ֑הּ תְּנֻ֤ד חֵֽיוְתָא֙ מִן־תַּחְתּ֔וֹהִי וְצִפְּרַיָּ֖א מִן־עַנְפֽוֹהִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Proclaiming with strength and thus saying: Cut down the tree and cut off its branches, strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit; let flee the beasts from under it, and the birds from its branches.

en.L: He was proclaiming with strength and saying thus: 'Hew down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.
en.B: He shouted in a loud voice: 'Fell the tree and lop off its branches; strip away its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.
en.R: He shouted, 'Chop down the tree and cut off its branches! Pull off its leaves and throw its fruit everywhere! Make the animals run away from under it, and make the birds fly away from its branches!

pt.L: Ele proclamava com força e dizia assim: 'Derrubem a árvore e cortem os seus ramos; arranquem a sua folhagem e espalhem o seu fruto. Fujam os animais de debaixo dela, e as aves dos seus ramos.
pt.B: Ele gritou em alta voz: 'Derrubem a árvore e cortem os seus galhos; arranquem as suas folhas e espalhem os seus frutos. Que os animais fujam de debaixo dela, e as aves dos seus galhos.
pt.R: Ele gritou: 'Derrubem a árvore e cortem os seus galhos! Arranquem as suas folhas e joguem os seus frutos para todo lado! Façam os animais fugirem de debaixo dela e as aves voarem dos seus galhos!

decisions.choice: cut down ... cut off ... strip off ... scatter: orders to other heavenly servants
decisions.reason: The commands are plural: the watcher gives orders to others, perhaps the heavenly servants who carry out God's decisions.

decisions.choice: let the animals flee and the birds: the peoples lose their shelter
decisions.reason: As the tree's shade and branches stood for the king's care for his peoples (verse 9), their flight shows the end of his rule.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the watcher's words
decisions.reason: The watcher's words are quoted inside the king's words to Daniel, which opened in verse 6, so they take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Derrubem, cortem, arranquem, espalhem (plural)
decisions.reason: The watcher's orders are plural, to other heavenly servants (m1), so Portuguese uses the plural imperative of "vocês"; "vós" forms are not used.

source.text: בְּרַ֨ם עִקַּ֤ר שָׁרְשׁ֨וֹהִי֙ בְּאַרְעָ֣א שְׁבֻ֔קוּ וּבֶֽאֱסוּר֙ דִּֽי־פַרְזֶ֣ל וּנְחָ֔שׁ בְּדִתְאָ֖א דִּ֣י בָרָ֑א וּבְטַ֤ל שְׁמַיָּא֙ יִצְטַבַּ֔ע וְעִם־חֵיוְתָ֥א חֲלָקֵ֖הּ בַּעֲשַׂ֥ב אַרְעָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: However, the stump of its roots in the earth leave, and with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; and with the dew of the heavens let it be wet, and with the beasts [be] its portion in the grass of the earth.

en.L: But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. And let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and with the animals [be] his portion in the grass of the earth.
en.B: But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let him share the lot of the animals in the grass of the earth.
en.R: But leave the stump and its roots in the ground. Put a band of iron and bronze around it, and leave it in the grass of the field. Let him get wet with the dew every morning, and let him live among the animals and eat grass.

pt.L: Mas deixem o toco das suas raízes na terra, com uma cinta de ferro e de bronze, na erva do campo. E que ele seja molhado com o orvalho dos céus, e com os animais [seja] a sua porção na erva da terra.
pt.B: Mas deixem na terra o toco com as suas raízes, preso com uma cinta de ferro e de bronze, na erva do campo. Que ele fique encharcado com o orvalho do céu e que tenha a mesma sorte dos animais na erva da terra.
pt.R: Mas deixem o toco e as suas raízes na terra. Ponham uma cinta de ferro e de bronze em volta dele e deixem-no na grama do campo. Que ele fique molhado com o orvalho toda manhã e que viva no meio dos animais, comendo capim.

decisions.choice: the stump of its roots: a sign of hope
decisions.reason: The tree is cut down but not uprooted. Verse 23 explains: the king's kingdom will be kept for him and given back. Isaiah uses the same picture of a stump from which new life comes (Isaiah 6:13; 11:1).

decisions.choice: let him be wet ... his portion: the picture moves from the tree to a man
alternatives: let it be wet ... its portion
decisions.reason: Partway through the verse the Aramaic stops speaking of a tree and speaks of someone who is wet with dew and lives among the animals. The words can be read "it" or "him"; what follows (verse 13) makes plain that a person is meant. The band of iron and bronze may protect the stump, or may picture the king bound in his madness; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: him ... his (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: From the dew onward, the English uses "him" and "his", since the person the tree stands for comes into view (m2). Readable adds "every morning" to show what being wet with dew means, and says "eat grass" for his portion in the grass.

decisions.choice: o toco ... ele
decisions.reason: "Toco" is masculine, so the "ele" of the second half can be read of the stump or of the man it stands for, as the Aramaic moves from the tree to a person (m2) without saying so; Portuguese keeps that shift with no added word, where English has to change from "it" to "him".

source.text: לִבְבֵהּ֙ מִן־אֲנָשָׁ֣א יְשַׁנּ֔וֹן וּלְבַ֥ב חֵיוָ֖ה יִתְיְהִ֣ב לֵ֑הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֥וּן עֲלֽוֹהִי׃

records.literal_gloss: His heart from [that of] a human let them change, and a heart of a beast let be given to him, and seven times let pass over him.

en.L: Let his heart be changed from [that of] a human, and let the heart of an animal be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.
en.B: Let his mind be changed from that of a human being, and let him be given the mind of an animal, until seven periods of time pass over him.
en.R: Let his mind be changed. Instead of thinking like a human being, let him think like an animal. Let him live this way for seven periods of time.

pt.L: Que o seu coração seja mudado de [coração] humano, e lhe seja dado um coração de animal, e passem sobre ele sete tempos.
pt.B: Que a sua mente seja mudada e deixe de ser a de um ser humano, e que lhe seja dada a mente de um animal, até que passem sobre ele sete períodos de tempo.
pt.R: Que a mente dele seja mudada. Em vez de pensar como um ser humano, que ele pense como um animal. Que ele viva assim durante sete períodos de tempo.

decisions.choice: his heart ... the heart of an animal: his mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and understanding. The king will lose his human reason and live like an animal (verse 30), until his understanding returns (verse 31).

decisions.choice: seven times: seven periods, perhaps seven years
decisions.reason: The text does not say how long a "time" is. Many take it as a year, so seven years; others think of seasons, or of a full, complete period (seven being the number of completeness). The same word is used in 7:25 for "a time, times and half a time".

decisions.choice: mind (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mind" for "heart", since thought, not feeling, is meant (m1). They keep "seven periods of time", not "seven years", since the text does not say (m2).

source.text: בִּגְזֵרַ֤ת עִירִין֙ פִּתְגָמָ֔א וּמֵאמַ֥ר קַדִּישִׁ֖ין שְׁאֵֽלְתָ֑א עַד־דִּבְרַ֡ת דִּ֣י יִנְדְּע֣וּן חַ֠יַּיָּא דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֨יט עִלָּאָ֜ה בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֗אוּלְמַן־דִּ֤י יִצְבֵּא֙ יִתְּנִנַּ֔הּ וּשְׁפַ֥ל אֲנָשִׁ֖ים יְקִ֥ים עֲלַֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] decree of [the] watchers [is] the command, and [by the] word of [the] holy ones the matter, to the end that may know the living that rules the Most High over [the] kingdom of humankind, and to whomever he wills he gives it, and the lowliest of humans he sets up over it.

en.L: The command is by the decree of the watchers, and the matter by the word of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills, and sets up over it the lowliest of {{gender:people|men}}.'
en.B: This sentence is by the decree of the watchers, the verdict by the word of the holy ones, so that everyone living may know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, and even sets over them the lowliest of {{gender:people|men}}.'
en.R: The heavenly messengers have decided this. The holy ones have given this order. They want everyone to know that the Most High God rules over all the kingdoms of the world. He gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants to. He can even make the humblest person a king.'

pt.L: A ordem é por decreto dos vigias, e o assunto, por palavra dos santos, para que os viventes saibam que o Altíssimo domina sobre o reino da humanidade, e o dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer, e põe sobre ele o mais humilde dos {{gender:seres humanos|homens}}.'
pt.B: Esta sentença é por decreto dos vigias, a decisão, por palavra dos santos, para que todos os que vivem saibam que o Altíssimo domina sobre os reinos humanos e os dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer, e põe sobre eles até o mais humilde dos {{gender:seres humanos|homens}}.'
pt.R: Os mensageiros celestiais decidiram isso. Os santos deram esta ordem. Eles querem que todos saibam que o Deus Altíssimo governa sobre todos os reinos do mundo. Ele os dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer. Ele pode até fazer da pessoa mais humilde um rei.'

decisions.choice: by the decree of the watchers: the decision of God's heavenly court
decisions.reason: The decision is announced as the decree of the watchers and holy ones. In verse 21 Daniel calls it "the decree of the Most High". The picture is of God's council in heaven, where his servants share in announcing his will (1 Kings 22:19-22; Job 1:6), but the decision is his.

decisions.choice: the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind: the lesson of the chapter
decisions.reason: This sentence is the point of the whole story and is repeated in verses 22 and 29 and in 5:21. No human king holds power by his own right; God gives it to whom he chooses, even to the lowliest.

decisions.choice: watchers: the heavenly beings of verse 10
decisions.reason: On the word, see verse 10.

decisions.choice: the watchers ... the holy ones (L, B); the heavenly messengers ... the holy ones (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. The phrase "the lowliest of men" takes the gender setting, since the Aramaic word means human beings. Readable spells out what the purpose clause means, and adds "God" to "the Most High". The watcher's words end here, so the single quotation mark closes.

decisions.choice: o Altíssimo domina sobre o reino da humanidade (L); ... sobre os reinos humanos (B); o Deus Altíssimo governa sobre todos os reinos do mundo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter (verses 22, 29): the refrain (m2) keeps one wording at each level, as the English does. "O reino da humanidade" says "humankind" without the gender setting, as the English Literal; the setting goes on "o mais humilde dos seres humanos", where the English has it.

source.text: דְּנָה֙ חֶלְמָ֣א חֲזֵ֔ית אֲנָ֖ה מַלְכָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֑ר וְאַ֨נְתְּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֜ר פִּשְׁרֵ֣א׀אֱמַ֗ר כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י׀כָּל־חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכוּתִ֗י לָֽא־יָכְלִ֤ין פִּשְׁרָא֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי וְאַ֣נְתְּ כָּהֵ֔ל דִּ֛י רֽוּחַ־אֱלָהִ֥ין קַדִּישִׁ֖ין בָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: This dream I saw, I, King Nebuchadnezzar; and you, Belteshazzar, its interpretation tell, because that all [the] wise men of my kingdom not are able its interpretation to make known to me, but you are able, for a spirit of gods holy [is] in you.

en.L: This [is] the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. And you, Belteshazzar, tell [me] its interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom are able to make the interpretation known to me; but you are able, for a spirit of [the] holy gods [is] in you."
en.B: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means, for none of the wise men of my kingdom can explain it to me. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."
en.R: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, had. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means. None of the wise men in my kingdom can tell me. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

pt.L: Este [é] o sonho que eu, o rei Nabucodonosor, vi. E você, Beltessazar, diga a sua interpretação, porque nenhum dos sábios do meu reino é capaz de me fazer conhecer a interpretação; mas você é capaz, pois um espírito [dos] deuses santos [está] em você."
pt.B: Este é o sonho que eu, o rei Nabucodonosor, tive. Agora, Beltessazar, diga-me o que ele significa, pois nenhum dos sábios do meu reino pode explicá-lo para mim. Mas você pode, porque o espírito dos deuses santos está em você."
pt.R: Este é o sonho que eu, o rei Nabucodonosor, tive. Agora, Beltessazar, diga-me o que ele significa. Nenhum dos sábios do meu reino consegue me dizer. Mas você consegue, porque o espírito dos deuses santos está em você."

decisions.choice: all the wise men cannot ... you can: Daniel against the experts again
decisions.reason: As in chapter 2 and in 5:7-16, the wise men of Babylon fail, and Daniel, in whom is a spirit of the holy gods (verse 5), succeeds.

decisions.choice: and you: the Masoretes correct the spelling of the pronoun
decisions.reason: The written text spells the word "you" in a form the Masoretes read in the usual way. The difference is one of spelling only.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The king's words to Daniel, which began in verse 6, end here.

source.text: אֱדַ֨יִן דָּֽנִיֵּ֜אל דִּֽי־שְׁמֵ֣הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֗ר אֶשְׁתּוֹמַם֙ כְּשָׁעָ֣ה חֲדָ֔ה וְרַעְיֹנֹ֖הִי יְבַהֲלֻנֵּ֑הּ עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ חֶלְמָ֤א וּפִשְׁרֵא֙ אַֽל־יְבַהֲלָ֔ךְ עָנֵ֤ה בֵלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֔ר מָרִ֕י חֶלְמָ֥א לְשָֽׂנְאָ֖ךְ וּפִשְׁרֵ֥הּ לְעָרָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then Daniel, whose name [was] Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him. Answering the king and saying: Belteshazzar, the dream and its interpretation let it not alarm you. Answering Belteshazzar and saying: My lord, the dream [be] for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.

en.L: Then Daniel, whose name [was] Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king answered and said, "Belteshazzar, let not the dream and its interpretation alarm you." Belteshazzar answered and said, "My lord, [may] the dream [be] for those hating you, and its interpretation for your foes!
en.B: Then Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was dismayed for a while, and his thoughts frightened him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning frighten you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, if only the dream were about those who hate you, and its meaning about your enemies!
en.R: Then Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar, was shocked for a while. His thoughts frightened him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning frighten you." Belteshazzar answered, "Sir, I wish that this dream were about your enemies. I wish its meaning were about the people who hate you!

pt.L: Então Daniel, cujo nome [era] Beltessazar, ficou atônito por um momento, e os seus pensamentos o perturbaram. O rei respondeu e disse: "Beltessazar, que o sonho e a sua interpretação não perturbem você." Beltessazar respondeu e disse: "Meu senhor, [seja] o sonho para os que odeiam o senhor, e a sua interpretação para os seus adversários!
pt.B: Então Daniel, também chamado Beltessazar, ficou consternado por algum tempo, e os seus pensamentos o assustaram. O rei disse: "Beltessazar, não deixe que o sonho ou o seu significado assuste você." Beltessazar respondeu: "Meu senhor, quem dera o sonho fosse sobre os que odeiam o senhor, e o seu significado sobre os seus inimigos!
pt.R: Então Daniel, que também era chamado Beltessazar, ficou chocado por algum tempo. Os seus pensamentos o assustavam. O rei disse: "Beltessazar, não deixe que o sonho ou o significado dele assuste você." Beltessazar respondeu: "Meu senhor, eu gostaria que esse sonho fosse sobre os seus inimigos. Eu gostaria que o significado dele fosse sobre as pessoas que odeiam o senhor!

decisions.choice: Daniel ... the king: the story now speaks of the king as "he"
decisions.reason: From this verse to verse 30, the letter speaks of Nebuchadnezzar in the third person, as "the king". It returns to "I" in verse 31. Perhaps the king did not wish to tell the time of his madness in his own voice, or the letter quotes another account; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the dream be for those who hate you: may it come true for your enemies, not for you
decisions.reason: Daniel's courteous wish shows that he respects the king and does not want the dream to be about him. He knows that it is.

decisions.choice: appalled for a moment: stunned and dismayed
decisions.reason: The verb means to be stunned or horrified. "A moment" is literally "one hour", that is, a short time.

decisions.choice: Sir (R); My lord (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Sir" for "My lord", the plain courtesy of a servant to his master today, and turns the wish into "I wish".

decisions.choice: Meu senhor (every level)
decisions.reason: Daniel's courteous address (m2) is "meu senhor" at every level, as 2:29 sets for his speech to the king; Readable keeps it where the English says "Sir", since a bare "Senhor" with a capital would read as God.

source.text: אִֽילָנָא֙ דִּ֣י חֲזַ֔יְתָ דִּ֥י רְבָ֖ה וּתְקִ֑ף וְרוּמֵהּ֙ יִמְטֵ֣א לִשְׁמַיָּ֔א וַחֲזוֹתֵ֖הּ לְכָל־אַרְעָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, and its height reached to the heavens and its sight to all the earth,

en.L: The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, and whose height reached to the heavens and whose visibility [was] to all the earth,
en.B: The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, whose top touched the sky and which could be seen by the whole earth,
en.R: You saw a tree that grew bigger and stronger. Its top reached the sky, and it could be seen everywhere in the world.

pt.L: A árvore que o senhor viu, que cresceu e se tornou forte, e cuja altura chegava até os céus e cuja visibilidade [era] para toda a terra,
pt.B: A árvore que o senhor viu, que cresceu e ficou grande e forte, cujo topo tocava o céu e que podia ser vista pela terra inteira,
pt.R: O senhor viu uma árvore que ficou maior e mais forte. O seu topo chegava até o céu, e ela podia ser vista em todos os lugares do mundo.

decisions.choice: the tree that you saw: Daniel repeats the dream
decisions.reason: Daniel repeats the king's description (verses 8-9) before he explains it (verse 19). The repetition is the style of the chapter.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on to verse 19, so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma. Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְעָפְיֵ֤הּ שַׁפִּיר֙ וְאִנְבֵּ֣הּ שַׂגִּ֔יא וּמָז֨וֹן לְכֹ֖לָּא־בֵ֑הּ תְּחֹת֗וֹהִי תְּדוּר֙ חֵיוַ֣ת בָּרָ֔א וּבְעַנְפ֕וֹהִי יִשְׁכְּנָ֖ן צִפֲּרֵ֥י שְׁמַיָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: and its foliage [was] beautiful, and its fruit abundant, and food for all [was] in it; under it dwelt the beasts of the field, and in its branches lived the birds of the heavens,

en.L: and whose foliage [was] beautiful and its fruit abundant, and in which [was] food for all, under which the animals of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the heavens lived,
en.B: whose leaves were beautiful and its fruit plentiful, providing food for all, under which the wild animals lived and in whose branches the birds of the sky nested,
en.R: It had beautiful leaves and lots of fruit, enough food for everyone. Wild animals lived under it, and birds lived in its branches.

pt.L: e cuja folhagem [era] bela e o seu fruto abundante, e na qual [havia] alimento para todos, debaixo da qual habitavam os animais do campo, e em cujos ramos moravam as aves dos céus,
pt.B: cujas folhas eram belas e os frutos abundantes, que dava alimento para todos, debaixo da qual viviam os animais selvagens e em cujos galhos as aves do céu faziam ninho,
pt.R: Ela tinha folhas bonitas e muitos frutos, comida suficiente para todos. Os animais selvagens viviam debaixo dela, e as aves moravam nos seus galhos.

decisions.choice: under it the animals dwelt: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 9, with small changes of wording ("dwelt" for "found shade").

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 19.

records.literal_gloss: It is you, O king, who have grown great and strong; and your greatness has grown and reached to the heavens, and your dominion to [the] end of the earth.

en.B: that tree is you, O king! You have grown great and strong; your greatness has grown until it reaches the sky, and your rule extends to the ends of the earth.

decisions.reason: Daniel says it as plainly as Nathan said to David, "You are the man" (2 Samuel 12:7). The king's greatness is real, but the dream says that it will be cut down.

en.L: And as the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying, 'Hew down the tree and destroy it; but the stump of its roots leave in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; and let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and with the animals of the field [be] his portion, until seven times pass over him,'
en.B: And as for the watcher, a holy one, whom the king saw coming down from heaven and saying, 'Fell the tree and destroy it, but leave its stump and roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be soaked with the dew of heaven, and let him share the lot of the wild animals until seven periods of time pass over him,'
en.R: Your Majesty, you saw a heavenly messenger, a holy one, coming down from the sky. He said, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it. But leave the stump and its roots in the ground. Put a band of iron and bronze around it, and leave it in the grass of the field. Let him get wet with the dew every morning. Let him live with the wild animals for seven periods of time.'

decisions.reason: In verse 14 the sentence was announced as the decree of the watchers; Daniel says plainly that it is the decision of the Most High God himself.

decisions.choice: The Most High God has decided (R)

records.literal_gloss: And you they will drive away from humankind, and with the beasts of the field will be your dwelling, and grass like oxen they will feed you, and from the dew of the heavens they will wet you, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over [the] kingdom of humankind, and to whomever he wills he gives it.

en.L: You will be driven away from humankind, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field. You will be fed grass like oxen and be made wet with the dew of the heavens, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills.
en.B: You will be driven away from people and will live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and you will be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.
en.R: You will be forced to leave people and live with the wild animals. You will eat grass like a cow, and you will be wet with dew every morning. Seven periods of time will pass. Then you will understand that the Most High God rules over all the kingdoms of the world. He gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants to.

pt.L: O senhor será expulso do meio da humanidade, e a sua morada será com os animais do campo. O senhor será alimentado com erva como os bois e será molhado com o orvalho dos céus, e sete tempos passarão sobre o senhor, até que o senhor saiba que o Altíssimo domina sobre o reino da humanidade e o dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer.
pt.B: O senhor será expulso do meio das pessoas e viverá com os animais selvagens. Será obrigado a comer capim como o gado e ficará encharcado com o orvalho do céu. pt.R: O senhor será obrigado a deixar as pessoas e viver com os animais selvagens. Vai comer capim como uma vaca e vai ficar molhado com o orvalho toda manhã. Sete períodos de tempo vão passar. Então o senhor vai entender que o Deus Altíssimo governa sobre todos os reinos do mundo. Ele os dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer.

decisions.choice: they will drive you ... feed you ... wet you: you will be driven ... fed ... wet
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "they will" without naming who; it is the common Aramaic way of saying "you will be". It may also hint at the heavenly servants who carry out God's decree (verse 14).

decisions.choice: grass like oxen: he will live and eat like an animal
decisions.reason: The king will lose his mind and live in the open like a grazing animal (verse 30).

decisions.choice: you will be driven ... fed ... made wet
decisions.reason: Each level gives the Aramaic "they will" as a passive, which is what it means (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And that they said to leave [the] stump of [the] roots of the tree, your kingdom to you [will be] enduring from [the time] that you know that rules the heavens.

en.L: And that they said to leave the root-stump of the tree: your kingdom will be enduring for you from [the time] that you know that the heavens rule.
en.B: The order to leave the tree's stump and roots means that your kingdom will be given back to you as soon as you acknowledge that Heaven rules.
en.R: The messenger said to leave the stump and the roots of the tree. That means you will get your kingdom back when you understand that God in heaven is the one who rules.

pt.L: E, como disseram para deixar o toco das raízes da árvore: o seu reino será firme para o senhor desde [o momento] em que o senhor souber que os céus dominam.
pt.B: A ordem de deixar o toco e as raízes da árvore quer dizer que o seu reino será devolvido ao senhor assim que o senhor reconhecer que o Céu governa.
pt.R: O mensageiro mandou deixar o toco e as raízes da árvore. Isso quer dizer que o senhor vai receber o seu reino de volta quando entender que Deus, no céu, é quem governa.

decisions.choice: the heavens rule: God rules
decisions.reason: "The heavens" stands for God himself, a way of speaking that avoids saying his name directly. It is the only place in the Old Testament where it is used in this way, and it is common in later Jewish writings (compare "the kingdom of heaven" in Matthew).

decisions.choice: enduring: secure, kept for you
decisions.reason: The word means firm or lasting. The kingdom will be kept for the king and restored to him (verse 33).

decisions.choice: the heavens rule (L); Heaven rules (B); God in heaven is the one who rules (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the heavens". Balanced writes "Heaven" with a capital, as a name for God; Readable says "God in heaven" (m1).

source.text: לָהֵ֣ן מַלְכָּ֗א מִלְכִּי֙ יִשְׁפַּ֣ר עֲלָ֔ךְ וַחֲטָאָךְ֙ בְּצִדְקָ֣ה פְרֻ֔ק וַעֲוָיָתָ֖ךְ בְּמִחַ֣ן עֲנָ֑יִן הֵ֛ן תֶּהֱוֵ֥א אַרְכָ֖ה לִשְׁלֵוְתָֽךְ׃

en.L: Therefore, O king, let my advice be pleasing to you: and your sins by righteousness break off, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed; perhaps there may be a lengthening of your prosperity."
en.B: Therefore, O king, please accept my advice: break with your sins by doing what is right, and with your wrongs by showing mercy to the oppressed. Perhaps then your prosperity will continue."
en.R: So please, Your Majesty, listen to my advice. Stop sinning and do what is right. Stop doing wrong and be kind to poor people. Then perhaps everything will keep going well for you."

pt.L: Portanto, ó rei, que o meu conselho seja agradável ao senhor: rompa com os seus pecados pela justiça, e com as suas iniquidades mostrando misericórdia aos oprimidos; talvez haja um prolongamento da sua prosperidade."
pt.B: Portanto, ó rei, aceite o meu conselho: rompa com os seus pecados praticando a justiça, e com as suas maldades tendo misericórdia dos oprimidos. Talvez assim a sua prosperidade continue."
pt.R: Por isso, Majestade, por favor, ouça o meu conselho. Pare de pecar e faça o que é certo. Pare de fazer o mal e seja bondoso com os pobres. Então talvez tudo continue indo bem para o senhor."

decisions.choice: righteousness: doing what is right, perhaps giving to the poor
decisions.reason: The word *tsidqah* usually means righteousness, right conduct. In later Aramaic and Hebrew it came to mean giving to the poor, charity, and that sense may already be present here, beside "showing mercy to the oppressed". The ancient versions took it that way. Either way, Daniel calls the king to justice and mercy toward the weak.

decisions.choice: break off: put an end to, as one breaks a yoke
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to tear away or to redeem. Daniel urges the king to break with his sins.

decisions.choice: perhaps your prosperity will be lengthened: repentance may delay the judgment
decisions.reason: Daniel does not promise that the judgment will be cancelled, but hopes that it may be put off, as with Nineveh (Jonah 3:9-10) and with Ahab (1 Kings 21:29). In verse 26 the judgment falls a year later.

decisions.choice: be kind to poor people (R)
decisions.reason: The word means people who are poor and oppressed. Readable says "poor people"; Literal and Balanced "the oppressed". Daniel's speech, which began in verse 16, ends here.

decisions.choice: walking on the palace: on its flat roof
decisions.reason: Houses and palaces had flat roofs, where people walked in the cool of the day (2 Samuel 11:2). From the roof the king could see the city he had built.

decisions.choice: at the end of twelve months: a year after the dream
decisions.reason: The judgment did not come at once. The king had a year in which to take Daniel's advice (verse 24).

decisions.choice: [the roof of] (L); the roof of (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "on the palace"; Literal supplies "the roof of" in brackets, and Balanced and Readable without (m1). Balanced ends the verse with a comma, since the sentence runs on into verse 27.

decisions.choice: o terraço
decisions.reason: The palace's flat roof (m1) is "terraço", where one can walk; "telhado" suggests a sloping tiled roof.

records.literal_gloss: Answering the king and saying: Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for a royal house by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?

en.L: The king answered and said, "Is this not Babylon the great, which I have built as a royal residence by the strength of my power and for the glory of my majesty?"
en.B: the king said, "Is this not the great Babylon that I have built as a royal capital by my own mighty power and for the glory of my majesty?"
en.R: He said, "Look at this great city of Babylon! I built it as the capital of my kingdom. I built it by my own power to show how great and glorious I am."

pt.L: O rei respondeu e disse: "Não é esta a grande Babilônia, que eu edifiquei como residência real pela força do meu poder e para a glória da minha majestade?"
pt.B: o rei disse: "Não é esta a grande Babilônia que eu construí como capital real, pelo meu próprio poder e para a glória da minha majestade?"
pt.R: Ele disse: "Vejam esta grande cidade da Babilônia! Eu a construí para ser a capital do meu reino. Eu a construí com o meu próprio poder para mostrar como sou grande e glorioso."

decisions.choice: Babylon the great, which I have built: Nebuchadnezzar's building
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar rebuilt Babylon on a grand scale: its walls, palaces, temples and the Ishtar Gate. His own inscriptions boast of this work, in words much like these. The phrase "Babylon the great" returns in Revelation 14:8 and 18:2 as a name for a proud and fallen power.

decisions.choice: by my power, for my glory: the king's pride
decisions.reason: The king gives himself the credit that belongs to God, who gave him "the kingdom, the power, the strength and the honor" (2:37). The words "power" and "glory" here answer that verse.

decisions.choice: royal capital (B)
decisions.reason: "A house of the kingdom" means the seat of royal government; Balanced says "royal capital".

source.text: ע֗וֹד מִלְּתָא֙ בְּפֻ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א קָ֖ל מִן־שְׁמַיָּ֣א נְפַ֑ל לָ֤ךְ אָֽמְרִין֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֖ה עֲדָ֥ת מִנָּֽךְ׃

en.R: Before the king had finished speaking, a voice came from heaven. It said, "King Nebuchadnezzar, this is what will happen to you. Your kingdom has been taken away from you.

decisions.choice: a voice fell from the heavens: God answers at once
decisions.reason: The judgment comes while the boast is still being spoken. The voice gives no new decree but announces that the old one (verses 14, 22) is now carried out.

decisions.choice: the kingdom has passed from you: as good as done
decisions.reason: The verb form speaks of the loss of the kingdom as already complete.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L)
decisions.reason: The voice's sentence runs on into verse 29, so Literal ends the verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: tu, ti, teu
decisions.reason: The voice from heaven speaks God's sentence (m1), and God speaks to one person with "tu" in the Old Testament, so the voice says "tu" to the king at every level, where Daniel, a subject, said "o senhor" (verse 22). Verse 29 repeats Daniel's words in this form.

source.text: וּמִן־אֲנָשָׁא֩ לָ֨ךְ טָֽרְדִ֜ין וְֽעִם־חֵיוַ֧ת בָּרָ֣א מְדֹרָ֗ךְ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ לָ֣ךְ יְטַעֲמ֔וּן וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עִדָּנִ֖ין יַחְלְפ֣וּן עֲלָ֑ךְ עַ֣ד דִּֽי־תִנְדַּ֗ע דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֤יט עִלָּיָא֙בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖א יִתְּנִנַּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and from humankind they will drive you, and with the beasts of the field [will be] your dwelling; grass like oxen they will feed you, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that rules the Most High over [the] kingdom of humankind, and to whomever he wills he gives it.

en.L: and you will be driven from humankind, and your dwelling [will be] with the animals of the field. You will be fed grass like oxen, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills."
en.B: You will be driven away from people to live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses."
en.R: You will be forced to leave people and live with the wild animals. You will eat grass like a cow. Seven periods of time will pass. Then you will understand that the Most High God rules over all the kingdoms of the world. He gives them to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants to."

pt.L: e tu serás expulso do meio da humanidade, e a tua morada [será] com os animais do campo. Serás alimentado com erva como os bois, e sete tempos passarão sobre ti, até que saibas que o Altíssimo domina sobre o reino da humanidade e o dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer."
pt.B: Serás expulso do meio das pessoas para viver com os animais selvagens. Serás obrigado a comer capim como o gado, e sete períodos de tempo passarão sobre ti, até que reconheças que o Altíssimo domina sobre os reinos humanos e os dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer."
pt.R: Serás obrigado a deixar as pessoas e viver com os animais selvagens. Comerás capim como uma vaca. Sete períodos de tempo passarão. Então entenderás que o Deus Altíssimo governa sobre todos os reinos do mundo. Ele os dá a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer."

decisions.choice: the words of verse 22
decisions.reason: The voice repeats Daniel's interpretation (verse 22) almost word for word. The sentence is now carried out.

decisions.choice: the Most High rules: the refrain of the chapter
decisions.reason: The third time the lesson is stated (verses 14, 22).

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 22 at each level
decisions.reason: The voice repeats Daniel's words, so each level reuses its wording of verse 22.

source.text: בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֗א מִלְּתָא֮ סָ֣פַת עַל־נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר֒ וּמִן־אֲנָשָׁ֣א טְרִ֔יד וְעִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יֵאכֻ֔ל וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּ֥י שַׂעְרֵ֛הּ כְּנִשְׁרִ֥ין רְבָ֖ה וְטִפְר֥וֹהִי כְצִפְּרִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: At that moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and from humankind he was driven, and grass like oxen he ate, and from the dew of the heavens his body was wet, until his hair like eagles' grew long, and his nails like birds'.

en.L: At that moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: he was driven from humankind, and he ate grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until his hair grew long like eagles' [feathers], and his nails like birds' [claws].
en.B: At that very moment the word was fulfilled against Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from people and ate grass like cattle, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew as long as eagles' feathers and his nails like the claws of birds.
en.R: Right away, what the voice said happened to Nebuchadnezzar. He was forced to leave people. He ate grass like a cow, and he was wet with dew. His hair grew long like the feathers of an eagle, and his nails grew long like the claws of a bird.

pt.L: Naquele momento a palavra se cumpriu sobre Nabucodonosor: ele foi expulso do meio da humanidade, e comia erva como os bois, e o seu corpo era molhado com o orvalho dos céus, até que o seu cabelo cresceu como [as penas] das águias, e as suas unhas como [as garras] das aves.
pt.B: Naquele mesmo instante a palavra se cumpriu contra Nabucodonosor. Ele foi expulso do meio das pessoas e comia capim como o gado, e o seu corpo ficava encharcado com o orvalho do céu, até que o seu cabelo cresceu como as penas das águias, e as suas unhas como as garras das aves.
pt.R: Na mesma hora, o que a voz disse aconteceu com Nabucodonosor. Ele foi obrigado a deixar as pessoas. Ele comia capim como uma vaca e ficava molhado com o orvalho. O seu cabelo cresceu, comprido como as penas de uma águia, e as suas unhas cresceram, compridas como as garras de uma ave.

decisions.choice: the king's madness: not recorded outside the Bible
decisions.reason: No Babylonian record tells of such a madness of Nebuchadnezzar. A text found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Prayer of Nabonidus, tells of the last king of Babylon, Nabonidus, who was struck with an illness for seven years at the oasis of Teima and was helped by a Jewish exile; Babylonian records also say that Nabonidus stayed away from Babylon for about ten years. Some think that the story in Daniel and that account go back to a common tradition. The text of Daniel names Nebuchadnezzar.

decisions.choice: hair like eagles', nails like birds': he became wild and unkempt
decisions.reason: Living in the open for years, the king's hair and nails grew long and wild, like the feathers and claws of birds.

decisions.choice: eagles' [feathers] ... birds' [claws] (L); feathers ... claws (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says only "like eagles'" and "like birds'"; Literal supplies the nouns in brackets.

source.text: וְלִקְצָ֣ת יֽוֹמַיָּה֩ אֲנָ֨ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֜ר עַיְנַ֣י׀לִשְׁמַיָּ֣א נִטְלֵ֗ת וּמַנְדְּעִי֙ עֲלַ֣י יְת֔וּב וּלְעִלָּאָה֙ בָּרְכֵ֔ת וּלְחַ֥י עָלְמָ֖א שַׁבְּחֵ֣ת וְהַדְּרֵ֑ת דִּ֤י שָׁלְטָנֵהּ֙ שָׁלְטָ֣ן עָלַ֔ם וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ עִם־דָּ֥ר וְדָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And at [the] end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, my eyes to the heavens lifted, and my understanding to me returned; and the Most High I blessed, and the one living forever I praised and honored, whose dominion [is] a dominion everlasting, and his kingdom with generation and generation.

en.L: And at the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my understanding came back to me; \q and the Most High I blessed, \q and the one who lives forever I praised and honored, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dominion [is] an everlasting dominion, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom [is] with generation and generation.
en.B: At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was restored. \q Then I blessed the Most High; \q I praised and honored the one who lives forever. \q His rule is an everlasting rule, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom lasts through every generation.
en.R: When the seven periods of time were over, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up toward heaven, and my mind became normal again. \q Then I praised the Most High God. \q I gave honor to the God who lives forever. \q His rule will never end. \q His kingdom will last for all time to come.

pt.L: E ao fim dos dias eu, Nabucodonosor, levantei os meus olhos para os céus, e o meu entendimento voltou a mim; \q e eu bendisse o Altíssimo, \q e louvei e honrei aquele que vive para sempre, \q pois o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} domínio [é] um domínio eterno, \q e o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} reino [é] de geração em geração.
pt.B: Ao fim daquele tempo, eu, Nabucodonosor, levantei os olhos para o céu, e o meu juízo voltou. \q Então bendisse o Altíssimo; \q louvei e honrei aquele que vive para sempre. \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} domínio é um domínio eterno, \q e o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} reino dura por todas as gerações.
pt.R: Quando os sete períodos de tempo terminaram, eu, Nabucodonosor, olhei para o céu, e a minha mente voltou ao normal. \q Então louvei o Deus Altíssimo. \q Dei honra ao Deus que vive para sempre. \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} domínio nunca vai acabar. \q O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} reino vai durar por todos os tempos.

decisions.choice: I, Nebuchadnezzar: the king speaks in his own voice again
decisions.reason: After verses 16-30, told of him as "the king", Nebuchadnezzar speaks again as "I" (see verse 16).

decisions.choice: I lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my understanding returned
decisions.reason: The turning point: when the king looks up to heaven, acknowledging God, his reason returns. This is what "until you know that the heavens rule" (verse 23) meant.

decisions.choice: an everlasting dominion ... from generation to generation: the hymn of 3:33
decisions.reason: The king's praise repeats the closing lines of the letter's opening hymn (3:33) and echoes Psalm 145:13. The same words are used of the kingdom of the one like a son of man (7:14).

decisions.choice: set in lines from "I blessed"; the wording of 3:33
decisions.reason: The terms for Daniel set 4:31-32 in lines. The first part of the verse, the king's return to sanity, is one long colon in the Aramaic accents and stays on one line; the hymn that follows is set in lines. The last two lines take up the wording of 3:33 at each level, with "dominion" (L) and "rule" (B, R) for the Aramaic word here. Readable says "the seven periods of time" for "the days", and "my mind became normal again" for "my understanding returned".

decisions.choice: the wording of 3:33
decisions.reason: The lines repeat the hymn that opens the letter (m3), so Literal and Balanced reuse its Portuguese ("de geração em geração", "dura por todas as gerações"); the possessives take the deity_pronoun span, as in 3:33.

source.text: וְכָל־דָּיְרֵ֤י אַרְעָא֙ כְּלָ֣ה חֲשִׁיבִ֔ין וּֽכְמִצְבְּיֵ֗הּ עָבֵד֙ בְּחֵ֣יל שְׁמַיָּ֔א וְדָיְרֵ֖י אַרְעָ֑א וְלָ֤א אִיתַי֙ דִּֽי־יְמַחֵ֣א בִידֵ֔הּ וְיֵ֥אמַר לֵ֖הּ מָ֥ה עֲבַֽדְתְּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all [the] inhabitants of the earth as nothing [are] accounted, and according to his will he does with [the] host of the heavens and [the] inhabitants of the earth; and there is no one who can strike his hand or say to him, What have you done?

en.L: And all the inhabitants of the earth [are] accounted as nothing, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will with the host of the heavens \q and the inhabitants of the earth; \q and there is none who can strike {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand \q or say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} done?"
en.B: All the people of the earth count as nothing before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pleases with the armies of heaven \q and with the people of the earth. \q No one can hold back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand \q or say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} done?"
en.R: Compared with God, all the people of the world are nothing. \q He does what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants with the angels in heaven \q and with the people on earth. \q No one can stop {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q or ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do that?"

pt.L: E todos os moradores da terra [são] considerados como nada, \q e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz segundo a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} vontade com o exército dos céus \q e com os moradores da terra; \q e não há quem possa bater na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão \q ou {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizer: "O que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste?"
pt.B: Todos os moradores da terra são como nada diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer com os exércitos do céu \q e com os moradores da terra. \q Ninguém pode deter a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão \q nem {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizer: "O que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste?"
pt.R: Comparadas com Deus, todas as pessoas do mundo não são nada. \q Ele faz o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quer com os anjos no céu \q e com as pessoas na terra. \q Ninguém pode impedi-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} \q nem perguntar a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Por que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fizeste isso?"

decisions.choice: all the inhabitants of the earth as nothing: the words of Isaiah 40:17
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 40:15-17, where the nations are like a drop from a bucket and counted as nothing before God. The proud king now says the same of all people, himself included.

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens: the armies of heavenly beings
decisions.reason: "The host of heaven" can mean the stars or the angels who serve God (1 Kings 22:19; Psalm 103:21). Here, set beside the people of the earth, it means the heavenly beings, such as the watchers of verses 10-14.

decisions.choice: strike his hand: hold back his hand, stop him
decisions.reason: To strike someone's hand is to stop him from acting; the idiom is known in later Aramaic and Hebrew. "What have you done?" is the question of someone who calls another to account (Job 9:12; Isaiah 45:9; Ecclesiastes 8:4).

decisions.choice: set in lines; armies of heaven (B); angels in heaven (R)
decisions.reason: The verse is set in lines at the Aramaic accents. The second "inhabitants of the earth" is a short line of its own in Literal and Balanced, as the accents divide it. Readable says "angels" for "the host of heaven" (m2), and "stop him" for the idiom (m3).

source.text: בֵּהּ־זִמְנָ֞א מַנְדְּעִ֣י׀יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֗י וְלִיקַ֨ר מַלְכוּתִ֜י הַדְרִ֤י וְזִוִי֙ יְת֣וּב עֲלַ֔י וְלִ֕י הַדָּֽבְרַ֥י וְרַבְרְבָנַ֖י יְבַע֑וֹן וְעַל־מַלְכוּתִ֣י הָתְקְנַ֔ת וּרְב֥וּ יַתִּירָ֖ה ה֥וּסְפַת לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: At that time my understanding returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and my splendor returned to me; and my counselors and my nobles sought me, and over my kingdom I was established, and greatness surpassing was added to me.

en.L: At that time my understanding came back to me, and for the honor of my kingdom my majesty and my splendor came back to me. And my counselors and my nobles sought me out, and I was established over my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me.
en.B: At that same time my sanity returned, and my majesty and splendor came back to me, to the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles came looking for me; I was set over my kingdom again, and still greater power was given to me.
en.R: At that time my mind became normal again. My honor and glory as king came back to me. My advisers and my important officials came looking for me. I became king again, and I was even greater than before.

pt.L: Naquele tempo o meu entendimento voltou a mim, e, para a glória do meu reino, a minha majestade e o meu esplendor voltaram a mim. E os meus conselheiros e os meus nobres me procuraram, e eu fui restabelecido sobre o meu reino, e ainda mais grandeza me foi acrescentada.
pt.B: Naquele mesmo tempo o meu juízo voltou, e a minha majestade e o meu esplendor me foram devolvidos, para a glória do meu reino. Os meus conselheiros e os meus nobres vieram me procurar; fui posto de novo sobre o meu reino, e um poder ainda maior me foi dado.
pt.R: Naquele tempo, a minha mente voltou ao normal. A minha honra e a minha glória de rei voltaram para mim. Os meus conselheiros e os meus oficiais importantes vieram me procurar. Eu voltei a ser rei e fiquei ainda maior que antes.

decisions.choice: my understanding returned ... still more greatness was added
decisions.reason: God keeps the promise of verse 23: the kingdom is given back. The king who learned that God gives kingdoms receives his own back as God's gift.

decisions.choice: my counselors: the king's high officials
decisions.reason: The word, also in 3:24, 27 and 6:8, is a title for close royal advisers.

decisions.choice: I was set over my kingdom again (B); I became king again (R)
decisions.reason: "Established over my kingdom" means set back on the throne.

source.text: כְּעַ֞ן אֲנָ֣ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר מְשַׁבַּ֨ח וּמְרוֹמֵ֤ם וּמְהַדַּר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמַיָּ֔א דִּ֤י כָל־מַעֲבָד֨וֹהִי֙ קְשֹׁ֔ט וְאֹרְחָתֵ֖הּ דִּ֑ין וְדִי֙ מַהְלְכִ֣ין בְּגֵוָ֔ה יָכִ֖ל לְהַשְׁפָּלָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and honor the King of the heavens, for all his works [are] truth and his ways justice, and those who walk in pride he is able to bring low.

en.L: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and honor the King of the heavens, because all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds [are] truth and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways [are] justice, and those walking in pride {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to humble.
en.B: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and honor the King of heaven, because everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does is right and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways are just, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can bring down those who live in pride.
en.R: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise the King of heaven. I give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} honor and glory. Everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does is right and fair. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can humble anyone who is proud.

pt.L: Agora eu, Nabucodonosor, louvo, e exalto, e glorifico o Rei dos céus, porque todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} obras [são] verdade e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} caminhos [são] justiça, e os que andam com soberba {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é capaz de humilhar.
pt.B: Agora eu, Nabucodonosor, louvo, exalto e glorifico o Rei do céu, porque tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz é certo e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} caminhos são justos, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pode humilhar os que vivem com orgulho.
pt.R: Agora eu, Nabucodonosor, louvo o Rei do céu. Eu dou honra e glória a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Tudo o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz é certo e justo. E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pode humilhar qualquer pessoa orgulhosa.

decisions.choice: the King of heaven: God as the true king
decisions.reason: This title is used only here in the Old Testament. The king who called himself "king of kings" (2:37) now confesses that the true King rules from heaven.

decisions.choice: those who walk in pride he is able to bring low: the lesson of the letter
decisions.reason: The letter ends with the lesson the king learned: God humbles the proud (Proverbs 16:18; Luke 1:51-52). In chapter 5 Daniel reminds Belshazzar of it (5:20-22).

decisions.choice: prose
decisions.reason: The terms for Daniel set the letter's hymn in 4:31-32; this closing verse, though it praises God, is kept as prose, as the end of the letter. Readable splits it into short sentences.
